root_cause.text: A race condition in the SMB Direct RDMA receive credit management logic allowed the kernel to grant credits that did not physically exist due to a timing window between hardware buffer reception and completion processing when relying on calculated posted versus granted counts.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "The logic off managing recv credits by counting posted recv_io and granted credits is racy" and notes a window "where we grant credits, which don't really exist," while the patch fixes this by introducing a dedicated `credits.available` counter incremented in `smb_direct_post_recv_credits` and used atomically in `manage_credits_prior_sending`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The SMB Direct RDMA receive credit management logic in `transport_rdma.c` contained a race condition where relying on posted receive I/O counts instead of a dedicated atomic counter allowed granting credits that did not exist during the window between hardware reception and completion processing.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description explicitly states "The logic off managing recv credits by counting posted recv_io and granted credits is racy" and identifies the window "between receiving the incoming recv at the hardware and processing the completion in the 'recv_done' functions". The patch fixes this by introducing `atomic_add(credits, &sc->recv_io.credits.available)` in `smb_direct_post_recv_credits` and modifying `manage_credits_prior_sending` to use `atomic_xchg(&sc->recv_io.credits.available, 0)` to safely track available credits.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement grants receive credits by atomically adding lcredits to the send_io.lcredits.count without verifying that sufficient physical buffers actually exist. This creates the race condition where credits can be granted during the timing window between hardware buffer reception and completion processing, allowing more credits to be granted than physically available.

This statement decrements the pending count as part of the credit calculation logic.
